verdict_reason: Rejected. The Java-valid perturbation set contains multiple failing no-oracle counterexamples. The decisive failures are mechanism-shaped: Rust preserves the ampersand prefix in the AST but never consumes Note.parallel in sequence rendering, so a teoz grouped parallel note advances vertically where Java groups it with the preceding tile; and Rust's sequence note consumer grammar still rejects Java-valid quoted participant operands on prefixed notes. Additional combined/over-several cases expose horizontal layout gaps around merged notes, while the basic slash merge controls pass.

java_observations: FactorySequenceNoteCommand accepts optional PARALLEL "&" followed by optional VMERGE "/" before note, hnote, or rnote for single-line and multiline one-participant notes, then calls note.goParallel() and SequenceDiagram.addNote(note, tryMerge).
FactorySequenceNoteOverSeveralCommand uses the same PARALLEL then VMERGE prefix grammar for note, hnote, and rnote over two participants.
SequenceDiagram.addNote only merges when the immediately preceding event is Note or Notes; after any other event kind, slash appends an ordinary Note event.

NotesBoxes.ensureConstraints reserves half of each raw component preferred width before/after note participants and pairwise space between distinct adjacent note members for classic merged Notes layout.
In teoz, NoteTile.getEvent() returns the Note, and GroupingTile.mergeParallel tests tile.getEvent().isParallel(), so Note.isParallel() is semantically visible for grouped teoz notes.

A combined & / note that merges into a Notes event is more subtle than the account states: Notes extends AbstractEvent and does not override isParallel(), and NotesTile.getEvent() returns the Notes aggregate. The individual Note keeps its parallel flag, but the merged aggregate is not itself an event-level parallel tile.
rust_observations: sequence_note_prefix strips an optional leading '&' and then an optional leading '/' with whitespace in the Java order.
SeqParser::try_note computes merge_with_previous as try_merge && last event is Event::Note(_), which preserves Java's immediate-note predecessor rule for the flat Rust event stream.
The sequence note regex remains narrower than Java: it accepts only \w+(,\w+)* participant operands, not Java's [%pLN_.@]+ or quoted participant operand forms.
sequence::Note now serializes parallel and merge_with_previous fields, but rg over the renderer found no consumer for note.parallel; only merge_with_previous drives sequence layout.
The renderer reconstructs contiguous merged note groups from flat Event::Note entries and applies NotesBoxes-like spacing constraints before solving participant x positions.

The new note_component_preferred_width constants have adjacent Java-source comments for ComponentRoseNote/Hexagonal/Box preferred widths, but the teoz NotesTile path is not represented by the cited NotesBoxes-only layout model.

findings.title: Ampersand parallel survives parsing but is not rendered
evidence: Rust source search found Note.parallel only in parser/AST/tests and no renderer consumer.
Java teoz GroupingTile.mergeParallel uses tile.getEvent().isParallel(); NoteTile.getEvent() returns the Note.
parallel_teoz_group_hnote_mixed_case.puml fails with the Java hnote sharing the previous vertical band and Rust placing it one row later.
findings.conclusion: The implementation does not satisfy the account's requirement that ampersand parallel intent be preserved through downstream layout.

findings.title: Sequence note consumer grammar remains narrower than Java's prefix grammar
evidence: Java note commands accept participant operands matching [%pLN_.@]+ or quoted strings.
Rust SeqParser::try_note still uses a regex that captures only \w+(,\w+)* participants.
quoted_prefixed_participant_grammar.puml is Java-valid and fails because the prefixed quoted-participant note is not constructed by Rust.
findings.conclusion: The implementation is not a single canonical Java-compatible sequence note command parser; it still rejects Java-valid prefixed note operands.

findings.title: Combined/over-several merged note layout is incomplete, especially under teoz
evidence: combined_parallel_merge_teoz_group_over_several.puml fails with width 603px expected vs 511px actual and compressed merged-note/group geometry.
inline_prefix_spacing_case_matrix.puml and reversed_over_participants_merge_span.puml fail on rectangular over-several note width/text placement.
The account and Rust comments cite NotesBoxes.ensureConstraints, but Java teoz uses NotesTile for merged Notes and has separate positioning behavior.
findings.conclusion: The merged note layout model is not complete across the requested combined-prefix and participant-topology axes.

findings.title: Account overstates event-level parallel semantics for combined & / notes
evidence: Java Note.goParallel sets the member Note flag before SequenceDiagram.addNote.
When slash merges the note, Java replaces/appends into a Notes aggregate whose class does not override AbstractEvent.isParallel().
NotesTile.getEvent() returns the Notes aggregate, so teoz parallel grouping does not see the member Note.parallel flag through Event.isParallel().
findings.conclusion: The causal account should distinguish unmerged Note parallel semantics from merged Notes aggregate semantics before implementation is retried.

findings.title: No fixture-shaped logic found for the fresh perturbations
evidence: Searches for fresh filenames, payload text, and mechanism names found no shipping-code references.
The basic three-note slash aggregate, slash-after-message control, and compact no-space multiline aggregate all pass.
findings.conclusion: The rejection is due to remaining mechanism gaps, not detected fixture-specific special casing.
